statement: The weak-equivalence class W_X on M/X consists of arrows whose underlying arrow in M belongs to W.
gap_or_error: The PDF has σ(U) where the arrow is u.
repair: Read σ(u) in the definition; retain σ(U) in the diplomatic source.

statement: The class Fib_W contains isomorphisms and is stable under composition and arbitrary base change.
repair: Composition follows from composition of pullback functors; base change follows by regarding a weak equivalence over the new base as one over the old base.
notes: Footnote 120 asks that this proposition be supplied.

statement: Under only the assumptions of footnote 119, Fib_W is stable under retracts in the arrow category.
gap_or_error: Two-out-of-three does not imply retract closure of W, which the usual retract argument requires.
repair: Assume W retract closed, or omit this clause. Explicit counterexample: finite sets, W preserving cardinal parity, fibration with fibre sizes (1,3), and its retract with fibre sizes (1,2).
notes: The complete counterexample satisfies all the stated minimal assumptions.

statement: Define Ho_W^!(S)=(M/S)[W_S^{-1}].
notes: It accepts every object over S, but its raw base change is not automatically defined for all base maps.

statement: If f:S′→S is a W-fibration, raw pullback induces Ho_W^!(S)→Ho_W^!(S′).
repair: This is exactly the defining preservation condition followed by the universal property of localization.

statement: Construct inverse images on Ho_W^!(S) for arbitrary base maps, coherently in S.
repair: Axiom a permits transport of the arbitrary pullback pseudofunctor from Ho_W^lc(S); complete formula and coherence explanation in commentary.

statement: If M has a terminal object e and derived inverse images have been constructed, the homotopy fibre of X/S at p:e→S is p^*(ho^!_{W/S}(X/S)) in Ho_W(M)≃Ho_W^!(e).
notes: The terminal-object assumption is explicit and is used only for this ordinary-point specialization.

statement: Fib_W S is the full subcategory of M/S on objects whose structural map is a W-fibration.
An arrow u between objects of Fib_W S belongs to W_S^u iff for every T→S its pullback u_T belongs to W.
notes: The quantifier includes the identity base map, so W_S^u⊆W_S.

statement: Define Ho_W^lc(S)=(Fib_W S)[(W_S^u)^{-1}].
Every base map f:S′→S induces f^*:Ho_W^lc(S)→Ho_W^lc(S′), with the coherent contravariance inherited from pullback.
repair: Fib_W is pullback stable and the universal quantifier for W^u is stable under iterated pullback. Canonical pullback isomorphisms give the pseudofunctor coherence.

statement: Localizing the entire slice at universally W-equivalent maps is generally too difficult to use for the intended locally constant theory.
notes: A methodological observation, not a universal theorem of uselessness or a size assertion proved under the minimal axioms.

statement: For a full subcategory fibred over the bases and stable under pullback, evaluation at a generalized point T/S is pullback to T followed by forgetting the base, inducing φ_T on the corresponding universal localization.
repair: Each u in W_S^u evaluates to a W-map, so the composite descends by localization.
notes: Footnote 121 specifies the fibred-subcategory hypothesis.

statement: The locally constant theory should send every weak equivalence T′→T over S to an isomorphism φ_T′(ξ)→φ_T(ξ).
notes: This is the intended generalized-point invariance property.

statement: Taking the permitted objects to be Fib_W S ensures this generalized-point invariance.
repair: For a representative X→S, X×_S(-) preserves W by definition. The property is compatible with W_S^u-equivalent representatives and therefore descends.

statement: Ho_W^lc has arbitrary inverse images and homotopically invariant generalized fibres, whereas Ho_W^! accepts arbitrary objects but initially only has raw pullback along W-fibrations.
notes: Collects the two formal constructions, without yet identifying them.

statement: Axiom a: for every S, inclusion induces an equivalence Ho_W^lc(S)→Ho_W^!(S).
notes: It is proposed as the homotopy-fibre axiom; it is not deduced from pullbacks and two-out-of-three.

statement: Axiom a implies that W_S^u and the restriction of W_S to Fib_W S have the same strong saturation.
repair: Under the equivalence, a W_S-arrow is inverted and hence belongs to the strong saturation of W_S^u. The reverse inclusion follows from W_S^u⊆W_S.

statement: Axiom b: every W_S-map between W-fibrations over S remains in W after arbitrary base change over S, equivalently W_S^u=W_S on Fib_W S.
notes: This is stronger than equality of strong saturations under only the minimal assumptions.

statement: Axioms a and b will usually be satisfied and proved together.
repair: If W is strongly saturated, a implies b; a proof is supplied. No unconditional equivalence between a and b is asserted.
notes: The source expresses a practical expectation rather than a precisely quantified converse.

statement: For Cat with the previously specified localizer axioms, the ultrafibration condition plus W(4a′) supplies axiom b.
references: Source cross-reference to Chapter XII, manuscript p.53
notes: This invokes the earlier fibre-localizer result; no new proof occurs here. The present audit does not silently remove its localizer hypothesis.

statement: For Cat, W(4a) supplies the fibre-localization comparison; footnote 122 suggests W(4b) should suffice.

statement: A good theory requires enough W-fibrations to represent every object of every slice up to W-equivalence.
repair: This describes the essential-surjectivity part. Full faithfulness of the localization comparison is an additional content supplied, for example, by a coaugmented replacement.
notes: The phrase pour l’essentiel is explanatory, not an equivalence of formal axioms proved here.

repair: Under functorial coaugmented replacement into Fib_W S, restrict the replacement to F and use its localized unit on both categories.

statement: In practical cases verification of a should also establish c.
repair: The explicit replacement proof explains this practical expectation; it is not a proof of the unrestricted logical implication.

statement: Proposed data: classes Liss and Prop containing isomorphisms and stable under composition and pullback, perhaps with $\mathrm{Liss}\cap\mathrm{Prop}\subseteq\mathrm{Fib}_W$.

notes: Here $W_\omega$ is the historical minimal class generated by W(1), W(2 bis), W(3), defined in XII ms.14; it is not the notation for a truncation level.

statement: $Z(f)=(X\times I)\amalg_{X\times\{0\}}Y$, with maps $i_f:X=X\times\{2n\}\to Z(f)$ and $p_f:Z(f)\to Y$ induced by $f\operatorname{pr}_1$ and $1_Y$, satisfies $p_f i_f=f$.
repair: The map called $\alpha$ in the intervening display is the same canonical retraction denoted $p_f$ elsewhere.
notes: The two endpoint labels $\operatorname{inj}_0$ and $\operatorname{inj}_1$ refer to endpoints 0 and $2n$, not adjacent vertices.

statement: $i_f:X\to Z(f)$ is a Dwyer map, hence a $W$-cofibration.
gap_or_error: The explanatory sentence on ms.230 prints $Y\to Y\amalg X$, although $i_f$ has source $X$.
repair: Use the $X$-summand inclusion $X\to Y\amalg X$ followed by the pushout $j$ of $i_X$.
notes: Edition slip confirmed on PDF leaf 3 and retained.

statement: The two squares in the expanded mapping-cylinder diagram are both pushouts and pullbacks in Cat.
repair: Pushout along the full sieve $X\times\{0,2n\}$ identifies only the prescribed first endpoint, and creates no additional objects or arrows between objects of the second endpoint. The square on coproducts is checked componentwise.
notes: The drawn top and bottom squares, not an assertion that every categorical pushout is a pullback.

statement: The inclusion $X\times\{0\}\to X\times I$ is Dwyer and belongs to $W$; its pushout $s_f:Y\to Z(f)$ belongs to $W$, and therefore its retraction $p_f$ belongs to $W$.
repair: Use the forward gluing property for a trivial Dwyer map and then $p_f s_f=1_Y$ with two-out-of-three.
notes: The cylinder factorization is natural in commutative squares of functors, as follows directly from the pushout construction.

statement: The preceding equality between weak equivalences and universal weak equivalences on $W$-fibrations has a dual statement for $W$-cofibrations.
repair: Made precise and proved as Proposition 16.
notes: The equality is restricted to the indicated full subcategory of the slice/coslice.

statement: Proposition 16: if $S\to X$ and $S\to Y$ are $W$-cofibrations and $f:X\to Y$ is a map under $S$ belonging to $W$, then $X\amalg_S S^{\prime}\to Y\amalg_S S^{\prime}$ belongs to $W$ for every $S\to S^{\prime}$.
gap_or_error: The last sentence prints $Y_0^{\prime}\to Y$ in place of $Y_0^{\prime}\to Y^{\prime}$.
repair: Factor $S\to S^{\prime}$ as a $W$-cofibration followed by a weak equivalence and use the displayed three-row pushout diagram.
notes: The typo is editorial/source-level, not a gap in the argument.

statement: In the proof of Proposition 16, the map $f_0^{\prime}$ is in $W$, and both maps $X_0^{\prime}\to X^{\prime}$ and $Y_0^{\prime}\to Y^{\prime}$ are in $W$.
repair: The first assertion uses $S\to S_0^{\prime}\in\operatorname{Cof}_W$; the other two use pushout stability of $S\to X$ and $S\to Y$ and $S_0^{\prime}\to S^{\prime}\in W$.
notes: This records the three distinct uses of the cofibration hypothesis.

statement: Proposition 16 is formal in any category with the required pushouts and factorizations $(\operatorname{Cof}_W,W)$, for $W$ satisfying two-out-of-three.
repair: No categorical nerve or lifting-property axiom is used.
notes: Existence of the stated pushouts is implicit in the general formulation.

statement: Dually, in any category with the required pullbacks and factorizations $(W,\operatorname{Fib}_W)$, a weak equivalence between $W$-fibrations over $S$ is preserved by every pullback $S^{\prime}\to S$.
repair: Apply the opposite-category form of Proposition 16.
notes: This is an assertion about maps between fibred objects, not arbitrary maps in the slice.

statement: Is every strict pushout along a $W$-cofibration $W$-cocartesian in the categorical-integral sense of XII, definition 3, ms.131?
gap_or_error: The question prints a base-change arrow $S^{\prime}\to S$, opposite to the arrow required for its pushout.
repair: Use $S\to S^{\prime}$; the corollary on ms.239 answers the question affirmatively under the standing hypotheses.
notes: This is not an open question remaining at the end of the passage.

statement: To answer that question, it suffices to establish: pushouts along Dwyer maps are $W$-cocartesian; squares whose opposite sides lie in $W$ are $W$-cocartesian; and $W$-cocartesian squares compose.
repair: The factorization of $S\to S^{\prime}$ in the displayed two-square diagram reduces the general square to the first two cases, and composition finishes.
notes: The reduction is conditional on the three facts, all established in the succeeding pages.

statement: A categorical pushout along a Dwyer map is $W$-cocartesian.
repair: Factor its other leg as a Dwyer map followed by $W$. The first square is a union of open subcategories; the second has two opposite sides in $W$. Use the subsequently established pasting theorem.
notes: There is no circularity: Proposition 18 is proved independently by categories of elements and a closed-cover argument.

statement: A pushout square whose two incoming maps are open immersions is $W$-cocartesian.
repair: This is the earlier open-cover calculation invoked here. For $W_\infty$, the nerve is the union of the two nerves along their intersection, hence computes the homotopy pushout.
notes: This is used for the upper square, whose incoming arrows are both Dwyer inclusions.

statement: A commutative square with its two opposite vertical sides in $W$ is $W$-cocartesian; by interchange of the two source legs the analogous horizontal statement holds.
repair: For the integral $\mathcal X$ of the source span, the map $j_1:X_1\to\mathcal X$ lies in $W$ when $i_2$ does; the composite to $Y$ is $f_1\in W$, so the comparison $\varphi:\mathcal X\to Y$ is in $W$.
notes: The proof uses the previously established homotopy-invariance property of the span integral.
